clue.text: Crack that's vulgar, heartless

indicators.note: heartless asks for the central letter of the synonym to be removed

parts.note: vulgar in the sense of tawdry or tacky is cheap

explanation.surface: A rude, unkind wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A chap is a crack or split in the skin, as in chapped lips.

clue.text: Provided bed where traveller may have dismounted in 23 28

definitions.text: where traveller may have dismounted in 23 28

parts.note: to have provided the food is to have done it, so provided can mean did
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Someone supplied a bed for a weary traveller at a stopping point in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 28 is OXFORDSHIRE; DIDCOT is a major railway junction there, where a traveller might get off a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Didcot is a railway junction town in Oxfordshire where rail passengers change trains.

clue.text: Hopes are renewed when soldiers ride in Western

indicators.note: the soldiers ride into the middle of the rearranged letters
renewed suggests the letters are made over in a fresh order

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Hopes rise again when the cavalry come riding into the cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' rearranges HOPES ARE into HSEOPERA (H, S, E, O, P, E, R, A), and 'ride in' puts OR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse opera is a jocular name for a Western film full of cowboys on horseback.

clue.text: VIP turned up carrying boy in a famous 23 28 burial place

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the next piece inside it
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nob is an important or upper-class person
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A dignitary arrives with a youngster at a well-known grave in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the VIP word, and 'carrying' has it hold the boy. This Oxfordshire village is where Winston Churchill is buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladon churchyard in Oxfordshire is famous as the grave site of Winston Churchill.

clue.text: Pigment mentioned somewhere in 23 28

indicators.note: mentioned means the word is spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: bistre is a brown pigment made from soot

explanation.surface: A colour is named as coming from a spot in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: BICESTER, an Oxfordshire town, is pronounced 'bister', which sounds like bistre.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicester is a market town in Oxfordshire, so it is a place within that county.

clue.text: Twin soldiers in film

indicators.note: twin asks for the same piece to appear twice, side by side

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A pair of identical soldiers appear in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a 1958 musical film starring Leslie Caron.

clue.text: Everyone in church held together by a union committed to common purpose

parts.note: everyone is all

indicators.note: the letters for in and church are held together by the letter A placed within them

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: All the congregation are bound together by a shared marriage vow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held together by' puts A inside INCE to give IANCE, after ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a pact or league of parties joined for a shared goal.

clue.text: The extent of two 28s, perhaps

explanation.surface: How far a pair of horses can reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is SHIRE, a breed of horse; a span is a pair of matched draught horses harnessed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the full reach or extent of something, and also a matched pair of horses or oxen.

clue.text: "I love coming back to vote in the House" — one in the Commons

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
one is the Roman numeral I
to poll is to vote

indicators.note: coming back means the letters from I and love are read in reverse

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An MP declares affection for voting in Parliament as a member of the lower chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns I + O into OI. The definition plays on the House of Commons: the commons are the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi means the common people, the masses, which is a sense of the commons.

clue.text: Institute's mistake in 23 28 village

parts.note: I is an abbreviation for Institute; the 's joins it to what follows
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: An academic body blunders in a country village.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLIP is a village near Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Islip is a small village in Oxfordshire, a few miles north of Oxford.

clue.text: It sounds like a call for the end of 19 rams

indicators.note: it sounds like tells us that the spoken word is what counts, not its spelling

parts.words: a call for the end of 19
parts.note: 19 is WAR; pax is Latin for peace, the cry for an end to fighting

explanation.surface: Something like a summons signals the death of some male sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 refers to the answer at 19-across, WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something into a space is to pack it in tightly, crams being a synonym.

clue.text: One concerned about what people eat initiated changes

definitions.text: One concerned about what people eat

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of the preceding word are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A newly admitted member alters something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a professional who advises on nutrition and food intake.

clue.text: Record situation of someone losing at Wimbledon?

definitions.text: situation of someone losing at Wimbledon?

explanation.surface: Noting how a tennis player stands when behind in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament; a player who has lost a set is 'a set down'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down is to record in writing; at tennis, a player losing by a set is a set down.

clue.text: What sucker needs a politician?

explanation.surface: Asking what a gullible person requires from a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was a British Labour Foreign and Home Secretary; a sucker is also one who sucks a drink through a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tube is needed by someone sucking up a drink, and Jack Straw was a leading Labour minister.

clue.text: Grateful response of Joseph and Mary to Wise Men for gifts?

definitions.text: Grateful response of Joseph and Mary to Wise Men for gifts?

parts.words: Grateful response of Joseph and Mary to Wise Men for gifts?
parts.note: Joseph and Mary would say a casual British thank-you to the three kings; split differently, those two words make money received by a shop

explanation.surface: The Holy Family thanks the Magi for their presents.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks, and the Wise Men are traditionally three Kings, so 'Ta, kings' is the reply; takings are receipts.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money received, which the cryptic reading makes the thanks for gifts.

clue.text: Heather trails after child going to fashion place in 23 28

indicators.note: trails after places the heather piece behind the child piece

parts.note: a kid is a child
ling is a name for common heather
ton means fashion or style, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: A girl called Heather follows a youngster heading for a style destination.
explanation.walkthrough: KIDLINGTON is a large village just north of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidlington is a large village in Oxfordshire, home to Oxford's airport.

clue.text: Missionary has set up southern city, not northern town

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the remaining letters are read upwards
not removes the town's name from the city's name

parts.note: Salisbury is a cathedral city in southern England
Bury is a town in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: A missionary has erected a southern city but not a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes BURY from SALISBURY, leaving SALIS; 'set up' turns that into SILAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Silas was the companion of St Paul on his missionary journeys in the New Testament.

clue.text: Plant covering hard ridge

indicators.note: covering means the plant surrounds the next piece

parts.note: rape is a yellow-flowered crop plant, oilseed rape
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Vegetation conceals a tough ridge of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A raphe is a seam-like ridge in anatomy or botany, such as on a seed.

clue.text: Hairy thing in what Ruby Ferguson wrote, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear tells us to listen to the words rather than read them

parts.note: Ruby Ferguson wrote the Jill pony books, stories about horses for children

explanation.surface: Something hairy appears in a children's author's book, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby Ferguson was a British author of the 'Jill' pony-story books.
explanation.definitionFit: A ponytail is a hairstyle with hair tied at the back, literally a hairy thing.

clue.text: Amorous maiden denied being offensive

indicators.note: denied means the maiden is refused a place in the word

parts.note: warm can mean amorous or affectionate
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A passionate girl is refused, and takes it badly.
explanation.definitionFit: War is a military campaign, as is an offensive, both being noun senses of fighting.

clue.text: Where in 23 28 you'll see crop adjacent to pasture

parts.note: wheat is a cereal crop
a ley is land temporarily under grass for grazing

explanation.surface: A rural spot in the county where crops sit beside meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: WHEATLEY is a village east of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheatley is a village in Oxfordshire, so it answers where in that county.

clue.text: Thrive without love or brood?

indicators.note: without means the love letter is left out

parts.note: to do well is to thrive
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking whether to prosper without affection or to mope.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell on something is to brood over it, both meaning to think about it at length.

clue.text: Need time to see some of 23 28?

parts.note: want is need or lack
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone must spend time to see part of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town once in Berkshire, now in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a town in Oxfordshire, so it is a part of that county.

clue.text: The fellow in America with nothing to hide is evil

indicators.note: to hide means the earlier pieces conceal nothing within them

parts.note: he is the fellow
taken as written
US is the United States
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An American man with nothing to conceal is wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' means the run fellow + in + America conceals the zero letter, rather than America hiding it alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous describes an act that is wicked or monstrous, a strong synonym for evil.

clue.text: Paula's last in race — will get/not get this

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the word for race

parts.note: to race is to hurry

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the name

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Paula Radcliffe's fate at the end of a marathon: a cheer, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: Paula Radcliffe was a British marathon runner; whether she wins the race decides whether she gets a cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheer is what a winning runner will get and a loser will not.

clue.text: Clinton was here (nothing wrong with former President)

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
X is the mark for a wrong answer
Gerald Ford was US President in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton was here, nothing amiss with an ex-President.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Clinton studied at OXFORD as a Rhodes Scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton spent time at Oxford University as a Rhodes Scholar.

clue.text: Feature of spa town that baby must be rescued from?

definitions.text: that baby must be rescued from?

explanation.surface: Something in a spa town from which a baby must be saved.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa town famous for its waters; the idiom warns against throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
explanation.definitionFit: The spa town Bath is noted for its water, and the idiom says not to throw the baby out with it.

clue.text: Man on the board neglecting work is a mistake

indicators.note: neglecting means the work is left out of the piece

parts.note: a bishop is a chess piece
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A director who skips his duties has erred.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British slang for a mistake or blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bish is informal British slang meaning an error or blunder.

clue.text: Plant, being little, died

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A tiny plant has perished.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is a plant, usually an unwanted one growing wild.

clue.text: Sports player losing pounds to become runner

indicators.note: losing means the pounds are dropped from the player

parts.note: a golfer plays the sport of golf
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A sportsman sheds weight and takes up running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is not an athlete but an errand-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer runs errands for others, so is an office runner.

clue.text: Woman at match not the first to make journey

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a bride is a woman at a match in the sense of a marriage

explanation.surface: A female spectator at a game travels, though not first.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle, to make a journey.

clue.text: Perhaps half of 3 shillings ahead of payment

indicators.note: ahead of places the shillings piece before the payment piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money
hire is payment for the use of something

explanation.surface: Half of three shillings comes before payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 3-down is HORSE OPERA; its first half, HORSE, is exemplified by a shire, a large draught horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire is a breed of heavy draught horse, an example of a horse.

clue.text: It's awfully rude getting on to two women in love

indicators.note: getting on to puts the rearranged letters after the two women

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
Mo is a woman's name, as in Mo Mowlam

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something crude is said about two women being smitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' signals the anagram and 'getting on to' sets it after the women; Ena and Mo are typical crossword names.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamoured means filled with love, besotted, which is to be in love.
